validity.recommendation: No change to LengthKnown (2623 km). The length_ratio flag (drawn route 1,228 km geodesic vs sheet 2,623 km, ratio 0.47) is a false positive from segment-vs-network granularity, not a wrong value or a RouteAccuracy problem. Independently verified: Petronas Gas Berhad's own corporate site states the PGU pipeline network it operates is '2,623-km' / '2,623 km' (https://www.petronas.com/pgb/our-business/gas-transportation) -- an exact match to the sheet value, from the asset's operator (primary source). GEM's routes-repo geometry (P1065.geojson, 25-part MultiLineString) traces a single corridor end-to-end from ~1.46N (Johor) to ~6.45N (Perlis border) at 1,227.7 km geodesic -- i.e. it IS the full-length mainline corridor, not a partial/truncated trace, but it is only the MAINLINE. Independent trade-press documentation (Oil & Gas Journal, 'Malaysia's Peninsular Gas system gets another segment') confirms PGU is built as mainline + parallel LOOP lines + LATERAL spurs, not one single pipe: Stage III alone is described as 448 km of 36-in mainline (Meru-Pauh) split into a 184 km Meru-Lumut sector (Sector 1) PLUS a 17 km 24-in lateral to Segari power station, and a 264 km Lumut-Pauh sector (Sectors 2-3) PLUS a 3 km lateral to the Gurun fertiliser plant and optional 21 km (Prai) and 25 km (Teknologi Tenaga Perlis) laterals. Separately, PGU 'Loop 2' is documented (Saipem/trade coverage) as a 230-km 36-in pipeline from Segamat to Meru laid PARALLEL to the existing mainline (i.e. adds pipe-km with zero new map extent) plus a 40-km upgrade of existing pipe; a 'Loop 1' (Kertih-Segamat) is referenced the same way. None of these loops or laterals are separately drawn in the routes-repo geometry for P1065. Summing a single-corridor mainline of ~1,200-1,300 km against a network that layers a second parallel trunk (Loop 1 + Loop 2) and half a dozen named lateral spurs (Lumut, Segari, Gurun, Prai, Teknologi Tenaga Perlis, plus Melaka/Port Dickson/Port Klang/Johor Bahru/Georgetown per the flag's own list) comfortably closes a ~1,400 km gap. Recommendation: stage a LengthKnown [ref] citing the Petronas Gas Berhad page (fill below); do NOT touch LengthKnown, LengthKnownUnits, or RouteAccuracy. If a researcher wants a tighter accounting than 'network total, corroborated', that requires digitizing the loop lines and laterals as additional routes-repo geometry (out of scope for this QC leg) -- but the flag itself is resolved as a non-issue.
validity.researcher_notes: Evidence trail: (1) Computed the drawn geometry myself: `../GOIT-GGIT-pipeline-routes/data/individual-routes/gas-pipelines/P1065.geojson` is a FeatureCollection of 25 MultiLineString parts spanning lon 100.15-103.84, lat 1.46-6.45 (i.e. Johor in the south to the Perlis/Thai border in the north -- the full peninsula, not a partial trace); summed geodesic length = 1,227.7 km, matching the flag's 1,228 km. This confirms the geometry is a genuine end-to-end mainline trace, so the gap isn't a truncated/incomplete digitization. (2) Petronas Gas Berhad's own official site (operator of PGU, a primary/regulatory-equivalent source per confidence_tiers.md) states verbatim: 'the 2,623km Peninsular Gas Utilisation (PGU) pipeline network' -- https://www.petronas.com/pgb/our-business/gas-transportation (verified: HTTP 200, contains '2,623' and 'Peninsular Gas Utilisation'). This is an EXACT match to the sheet's existing LengthKnown=2623, from the entity that built and runs the asset -- sufficient alone for high tier per the rubric ('one primary/regulatory source'). (3) A second passage, from The Edge Malaysia ('Liberalising Natural Gas Market: Peninsular Malaysia's Journey', URL path content/advertise/... -- flagging this looks like sponsored/native content, likely PETRONAS-authored, so I am NOT treating it as a genuinely independent second source, just corroborating restatement), separately says 'the PGU boasts an impressive 2,623-kilometre high-pressure transmission pipeline network' and distinguishes it from the downstream 2,465-km NGDS distribution network -- useful for confirming PGU-vs-NGDS scope isn't the confusion, but not counted toward the 2-independent bar. (4) Oil & Gas Journal ('Malaysia's Peninsular Gas system gets another segment', verified HTTP 200) is genuinely independent trade press and gives concrete segment/lateral lengths for PGU Stage III (448 km mainline in two sub-sectors of 184 km and 264 km, plus 17 km, 3 km, and two ~21-25 km optional laterals) -- this doesn't restate the 2,623 km total but corroborates the STRUCTURE (mainline + laterals, built in stages) that explains why a single-corridor trace undercounts the network. (5) Wikipedia's 'Peninsula Gas Utilisation' article corroborates PGU was built in 3 phases (1984-2001) with laterals to Lumut and Gurun under Phase III, but is internally inconsistent (states both 2,623 km and, elsewhere, '2,500 kilometers') and cites a 1997 conference paper I could not independently retrieve -- used only for background, not cited as a ref. (6) Petronas' own Petrosains (science-outreach arm) posted a Facebook video captioned 'PETRONAS runs a 2623km Peninsular Gas Utilisation (PGU) gas pipeline network' -- same corporate origin as (2), not counted as independent, and Facebook is a poor ref format regardless. Could NOT establish: a published per-loop/per-lateral length breakdown that arithmetically reconciles 1,228 (mainline) + loops + laterals = 2,623 to the km -- the pieces I found (Loop 2 = 230 km + 40 km upgrade; Stage III laterals totaling roughly 40-65 km) are consistent with, but don't fully prove, the exact 2,623 figure. Given the operator's own primary-source statement matches the sheet exactly, and the network is independently documented to include a second parallel loop trunk plus multiple named laterals not drawn in the current geometry, I'm confident this is a segment(mainline)-vs-network flag, not a data error -- but a full km-by-km reconciliation of loops+laterals would need someone to digitize that geometry, which is beyond this QC leg. For the record only (deep-sweep leg already flagged, not researched here per instructions): StartYear1=1993 doesn't match any phase-completion date I saw (1984/1992/1998/2001 all appear instead); Owner1 'Petronas 100%' is likely more precisely Petronas Gas Berhad, PGB's own pages describe it as the network operator and PGB is a separately-listed, not-wholly-Petronas-owned subsidiary.

summary: The length_ratio flag (GEM route geometry 1,228 km vs sheet LengthKnown 2,623 km) is a false positive: the routes-repo geometry is a genuine, complete end-to-end trace of the PGU mainline corridor (Johor to Perlis, confirmed by computing its own geodesic length), while 2,623 km is the PGU network total including parallel loop lines (Loop 1 Kertih-Segamat, Loop 2 Segamat-Meru at 230 km) and multiple named laterals (Lumut, Segari, Gurun, Prai, Teknologi Tenaga Perlis, etc.) that are not drawn in this single geometry. Petronas Gas Berhad's own site states the network is '2,623km', an exact match and a primary-source confirmation (high tier); Oil & Gas Journal independently corroborates the mainline+loop+lateral network structure. Recommendation: no value change; stage a LengthKnown [ref] confirming 2623 as high-tier.
